reason: The mirror of the publication's counters onto the copy's rows allocates once, the array their node lists are cut from, in place of two allocations per Instance: 3,093 / 12,141 / 1,203 allocations at 1,000 and 4,000 single-pod Instances and 160 gangs of eight, from 5,097 / 20,157 / 1,525; the bytes 460 KB / 1.81 MB / 203 KB from 688 KB / 2.73 MB / 237 KB. The availability reading sizes its set of names from the endpoint count instead of growing the map from nothing (the slices are served uncopied here, so the reading's other saving, the cache's copy of every slice, is not in this count): gang/160x8/allocations 1,541 → 1,525 and gang/160x8/bytes 291,200 → 236,856 (the fixture publishes every pod of a gang, 1,280 endpoints, so the map's growth was a fifth of the write's bytes at this shape), readySince/1000/allocations 5,113 → 5,097 and bytes 742,744 → 688,400, readySince/4000/allocations 20,187 → 20,157 and bytes 2,944,248 → 2,726,080. The write groups the pods by Instance, to recompute the published fields, from one array after one count per Instance: 5,113 / 20,187 / 1,541 allocations at 1,000 and 4,000 single-pod Instances and 160 gangs of eight, from 6,126 / 24,214 / 2,187 with one slice per Instance and the map grown from nothing; the bytes 743 KB / 2.94 MB / 291 KB from 809 KB / 3.22 MB / 298 KB. The status write at the end of one pass over a replica at rest, every Instance Ready on the spec revision with every pod serving and a Ready endpoint, the pods and the EndpointSlices served from memory uncopied and every Node present, so the count is the write's own. The write recomputes the published fields over the pods on a copy of the pass's own status and finds it equal, so nothing is read live or written: the live object is read only when the copy calls for a write. The compare that finds it equal reads the rows field by field; while it walked them by reflection the write cost 37,186 allocations and 2.5 MB at 1,000 Instances, 148,384 and 10.0 MB at 4,000, 7,174 and 0.6 MB at 160 gangs of eight. Before the copy decided, the write read the replica live once per pass, the fake apiserver's JSON round trip of the whole object (200 KB at 4,000 rows), and converted the live rows: 43,347 allocations and 3.3 MB at 1,000 Instances, 172,556 and 13.8 MB at 4,000, 8,299 and 0.7 MB at 160 gangs of eight. The deadline step the write runs last (reconcileHeldDeadlines) converts only the rows with an operation open and reads nothing at rest, where no row has one: gang/160x8/allocations 2,999 → 2,348, gang/160x8/bytes 451,752 → 334,560, readySince/1000/allocations 11,140 → 7,127, readySince/1000/bytes 1,522,064 → 1,029,152, readySince/4000/allocations 44,240 → 28,215, readySince/4000/bytes 6,021,520 → 4,084,656. The decision on the copy compares the rows with their publication in place and deep-copies no row: gang/160x8/allocations 2,348 → 2,187, gang/160x8/bytes 334,560 → 297,952, readySince/1000/allocations 7,127 → 6,126, readySince/1000/bytes 1,029,152 → 808,544, readySince/4000/allocations 28,215 → 24,214, readySince/4000/bytes 4,084,656 → 3,218,608. Re-recorded with the status write reading the pass's list's buckets by Instance, built once per list by the first reader of the pass (the engine's observation in a pass; the first status write of the fixture here), instead of bucketing the pods on every write: 3,093 / 12,141 / 1,203 to 3,084 / 12,120 / 1,196 allocations and 460 KB / 1.81 MB / 203 KB to 357 KB / 1.40 MB / 171 KB at 1,000 and 4,000 single-pod Instances and 160 gangs of eight; the live reads and the writes stand at none. Re-recorded with the publication building no list per Instance (status.AppendUniqueNodes cuts every row's node list from one array, the pods that report are read in place when none is left out, and the live pods are counted without a list): gang/160x8/allocations 1,196 → 240, gang/160x8/bytes 171,192 → 143,088, readySince/1000/allocations 3,084 → 1,086, readySince/1000/bytes 357,312 → 349,704, readySince/4000/allocations 12,120 → 4,122, readySince/4000/bytes 1,401,872 → 1,371,416; the live reads stay at zero.
